stimulus.body: A transit planner's board lists 88.0 g of CO2 and molar mass 44.0 g/mol.

questions.stem: How many moles of CO2 is that?
questions.explanation: 88.0 g / 44.0 g/mol = 2.00 mol. Divide mass by molar mass. Option B halves. Option C inverts. Option D confuses grams with moles.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Convert moles to mass using molar mass

stimulus.body: A transit planner's board shows 2.50 mol of CaCO3 and molar mass 100.0 g/mol.

questions.stem: What mass of CaCO3 results?
questions.explanation: 2.50 mol times 100.0 g/mol equals 250.0 g. Multiply moles by molar mass. Option B divides. Option C uses one mole. Option D confuses units.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Convert mass to a particle count via moles

stimulus.body: A transit planner's board lists 16.0 g of CH4 and molar mass 16.0 g/mol.

questions.stem: How many CH4 molecules is that?
questions.explanation: 16.0 g / 16.0 g/mol = 1.00 mol, giving 6.022e23 molecules. Option B doubles. Option C stops at moles. Option D skips the mole step.
questions.hint: Convert grams to moles, then to molecules.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Convert a particle count to mass via moles

stimulus.body: A transit planner's board lists 6.022e23 N2 molecules and molar mass 28.0 g/mol.

questions.stem: What mass of N2 results?
questions.explanation: 6.022e23 molecules is 1.00 mol. Times 28.0 g/mol = 28.0 g. Option B uses atomic nitrogen. Option C doubles. Option D skips the mole step.
questions.hint: Convert particles to moles, then to grams.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Count atoms per formula unit
questions.stem: A transit planner reads Na2CO3 on the board; how many atoms per formula unit?
questions.explanation: Na2CO3 has 2 Na, 1 C, and 3 O, totaling 6 atoms. Option B counts symbols. Option C misses an oxygen. Option D adds an extra oxygen.
